paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Predicting narrative frames using oracle (human-annotated) and noisy (predicted) labels for their , , , and ; the results are macro-averaged F1.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the macro-averaged F1 scores for predicting narrative frames using three different language models—Gemini, GPT4o, and Sonnet—under three distinct prompting strategies: "Basic prompt" (dark blue), "Structured prompt + oracle" (orange), and "Structured prompt + predicted" (dark green). The horizontal axis categorizes the models, arranged in the order Gemini, GPT4o, and Sonnet, while the vertical axis represents the F1 score on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 0.7, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. For each model, the orange bar (Structured prompt + oracle) consistently achieves the highest F1 score, with values approximately 0.6 for Gemini, 0.58 for GPT4o, and 0.52 for Sonnet. The dark green bars (Structured prompt + predicted) show lower but still substantial performance, with scores around 0.36 for Gemini, 0.48 for GPT4o, and 0.42 for Sonnet. The dark blue bars (Basic prompt) are the shortest in each group, with scores approximately 0.32 for Gemini, 0.25 for GPT4o, and 0.33 for Sonnet. The chart visually emphasizes that using structured prompts with oracle labels yields the best performance across all models, while basic prompting performs the worst, and structured prompts with predicted labels offer an intermediate improvement. No bars are annotated or visually emphasized beyond their color-coding, and the data is presented without error bars or confidence intervals.
